title: Once Correct, Still Wrong: Counterfactual Hallucination in Multilingual Vision-Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating models on the culturally grounded M2CQA benchmark to calculate the CounterFactual Hallucination Rate (CFHR), which measures how often models accept culturally plausible but visually unsupported counterfactual statements about the MENA region based on stereotypic priors.

Comparing model accuracy and counterfactual hallucination rates (CFHR) across English, Modern Standard Arabic (MSA), and lower-resource Arabic dialects (Egyptian and Levantine) to assess how linguistic uncertainty affects multimodal reasoning.
